nahw-129.meaning: the describing word in a <bdi>التَّوْصِيفِيّ</bdi> phrase

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: the incomplete verbs — <bdi>كَانَ</bdi> and her sisters

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.text: <bdi>كَانَ</bdi> and her sisters keep the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> in {{c1::<bdi>رَفْع</bdi>}}, as {{c2::<bdi>اِسْم كَانَ</bdi>}}, and put the <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> in {{c3::<bdi>نَصْب</bdi>}}, as {{c4::<bdi>خَبَر كَانَ</bdi>}}
nahw.extra: Each takes its own verb's name: <bdi>اِسْم صَارَ</bdi>, <bdi>خَبَر لَيْسَ</bdi>, and so on.

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.text: {{c1::<bdi>كَانَ</bdi>}} and her sisters keep the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> in <bdi>رَفْع</bdi> and put the <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> in <bdi>نَصْب</bdi>; {{c2::<bdi>إِنَّ</bdi>}} and her sisters do the reverse — the <bdi>مُبْتَدَأ</bdi> in <bdi>نَصْب</bdi>, the <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> in <bdi>رَفْع</bdi>
nahw.extra: One family is verbs, the other particles — and their effects are mirror images.

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.front: When <bdi>كَانَ</bdi> or one of her sisters is used as an ordinary verb, what is it called?

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.front: What does <bdi>كَانَ</bdi> give a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> that follows it?
nahw.back: A past continuous or habitual meaning — <bdi>كَانَ يَكْتُبُ</bdi>, “he was writing” or “he used to write”

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: became — going from one state to another; a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: to happen in the morning — or simply “became”; a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: to happen in the evening — or simply “became”; a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: to happen at midmorning — or simply “became”; a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: to happen during the day — or simply “became”; a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: to happen during the night — or simply “became”; a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: as long as — a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.text: Four sisters of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi> mean “always, continuously”: {{c1::<bdi>مَا زَالَ</bdi>}}, {{c2::<bdi>مَا بَرِحَ</bdi>}}, {{c3::<bdi>مَا فَتِئَ</bdi>}}, {{c4::<bdi>مَا انْفَكَّ</bdi>}}
nahw.extra: Same meaning, so they are learned as one set rather than as four cards with one gloss.

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.front: What do <bdi>مَا زَالَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَا بَرِحَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَا فَتِئَ</bdi> and <bdi>مَا انْفَكَّ</bdi> mean, as sisters of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>?
nahw.back: Always, continuously — all four mean the same

nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch. 1 — the fiʿl: kāna and her sisters — class notes (in Notion by 2026-10-02)
nahw.meaning: is not, not — a sister of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>

nahw.front: Which of <bdi>كَانَ</bdi>'s sisters have only a past tense?

nahw.front: What is sometimes prefixed to the <bdi>خَبَر</bdi> of <bdi>لَيْسَ</bdi>?

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: The <bdi>أَمْر</bdi>, the imperative, is formed for which person only?

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.text: To form the <bdi>أَمْر</bdi> of a family-one verb from its <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>: {{c1::remove the <bdi>حَرْف المُضَارِع</bdi>}}; {{c2::add a <bdi>هَمْزَة الوَصْل</bdi>}}; {{c3::make the ending <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>}}

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: When does the <bdi>هَمْزَة الوَصْل</bdi> of the <bdi>أَمْر</bdi> take a ḍammah?
sarf.back: When the verb's <bdi>عَيْن</bdi> has a ḍammah — <bdi>اُنْصُرْ</bdi>; otherwise it takes a kasrah — <bdi>اِضْرِبْ</bdi>, <bdi>اِفْتَحْ</bdi>

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: How is a command — “he should …” — given to the third person?
sarf.back: With <bdi>لَام الأَمْر</bdi>: a <bdi>لَام</bdi> with a kasrah before the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>, which it makes <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi> — <bdi>لِيَنْصُرْ</bdi>, “let him help”

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: What vowel does <bdi>لَام الأَمْر</bdi> take after <bdi>وَ</bdi> or <bdi>فَـ</bdi>?

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.text: <bdi>لَام الأَمْر</bdi> works with passive verbs too: from <bdi>لِيَنْصُرْ</bdi>, “let him help”, comes {{c1::<bdi>لِيُنْصَرْ</bdi>}}, “let him be helped”

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: How is the <bdi>نَهْي</bdi>, the negative command, formed?
sarf.back: Put <bdi>لَا النَّاهِيَة</bdi> before the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> and make it <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi> — <bdi>لَا تَنْصُرْ</bdi>

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.text: Before a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>, {{c1::<bdi>لَا النَّاهِيَة</bdi>}} makes it <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi> — a prohibition; {{c2::<bdi>لَا النَّافِيَة</bdi>}} leaves it as it is — a negation
sarf.extra: <bdi>لَا تَنْصُرْ</bdi>, “don't help”; <bdi>لَا تَنْصُرُ</bdi>, “you don't help” or “you won't help”.

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: In what sense are <bdi>اِسْم الفَاعِل</bdi> and <bdi>اِسْم المَفْعُول</bdi> each a <bdi>صِفَة</bdi>?
sarf.back: As descriptive words — not the <bdi>صِفَة</bdi> of a <bdi>تَوْصِيفِيّ</bdi> phrase in naḥw

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the active participle — a derived noun for the doer of the action, e.g. <bdi>نَاصِر</bdi>

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the passive participle — a derived noun for the one the action is done to, e.g. <bdi>مَنْصُور</bdi>

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: How do <bdi>اِسْم الفَاعِل</bdi> and <bdi>اِسْم المَفْعُول</bdi> behave grammatically?
sarf.back: Like any <bdi>اِسْم</bdi> — they follow its rules and are inflected like one

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.text: {{c1::<bdi>الفَاعِل</bdi>}} is the doer as a part of a verbal sentence — a naḥw role; {{c2::<bdi>اِسْم الفَاعِل</bdi>}} is a derived noun that names the doer — a ṣarf pattern
sarf.extra: Same root word, two sciences, two different things.

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the adjective resembling the active participle — a long-term or intrinsic quality; an emphatic way of being the doer

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.text: Common patterns of <bdi>الصِّفَة المُشَبَّهَة</bdi>: {{c1::<bdi>فَعِيل</bdi>}}, {{c2::<bdi>فَعُول</bdi>}}, and {{c3::<bdi>فَعْلَان</bdi>}}, feminine {{c4::<bdi>فَعْلَى</bdi>}}

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: In some cases, what can <bdi>الصِّفَة المُشَبَّهَة</bdi> stand for?
sarf.back: An <bdi>اِسْم المَفْعُول</bdi> — the one acted on, as a long-term or intrinsic quality

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the noun of exaggeration — a hyperbolic, emphatic adjective

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the noun of preference — the comparative and superlative, e.g. <bdi>أَكْبَر</bdi>, greater or greatest

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the noun of time or place — names when or where an action happens

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.meaning: the noun of instrument — a tool used for an action, e.g. <bdi>مِفْتَاح</bdi>, a tool for opening

sarf.source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf: the amr and nahy, the derived nouns — class notes 2026-10-08
sarf.front: What do <bdi>الصِّفَة المُشَبَّهَة</bdi>, <bdi>اِسْم المُبَالَغَة</bdi>, <bdi>اِسْم التَّفْضِيل</bdi>, <bdi>اِسْم الظَّرْف</bdi> and <bdi>اِسْم الآلَة</bdi> have in common?
sarf.back: Each is formed only from <bdi>ثُلَاثِيّ مُجَرَّد</bdi> verbs
